This enabled systematic comparison of cognitive impairment-relevant features across datasets and tasks. Our results revealed that acoustic features did not generalize uniformly across tasks and languages. Temporal features remained robust across all datasets, consistently capturing timing disruption regardless of language or task. In contrast, speech rate showed strong task dependence -- emerging as informative mainly in single-speaker tasks with externally anchored content and pacing, but becoming less reliable when speech content was highly individualized. Pitch-related features further exhibited language-specific patterns, favoring chroma-related features in tonal languages (e.g., Mandarin) and F0-related features in non-tonal languages. These findings caution against indiscriminate pooling of heterogeneous speech data and underscore the need for interpretable, context-aware approaches to multilingual dementia detection using automated speech analysis.

papers.title: Lower Bound of Thermal Conductivity in Graphene
papers.abstract: The intrinsic thermal conductivity ($κ$) of graphene remains highly controversial because of physical and metrological complexities. Although the thermal bridge method enables reliable measurements, sample fabrication remains challenging. Here, we develop a highly efficient patterning and transfer technique to systematically fabricate and characterize suspended bilayer graphene (BLG) thermal bridges with lengths of 1-30 $μ$m. Suspended BLG with unavoidable polymer residues exhibits length-independent thermal conductivity of approximately 570 W/(m K) at room temperature, remaining nearly constant from 250 to 350 K and robust to rigorous surface cleaning and amorphous silicon nitride substrates. Homogeneous non-equilibrium molecular dynamics (HNEMD) simulations show that amorphous carbon coverage of only approximately 0.01 monolayer is sufficient to suppress out-of-plane flexural acoustic (ZA) phonons. These findings challenge the prevailing view that rigid substrates suppress ZA phonons more strongly than surface contamination and identify a robust lower bound of $κ$ governed by amorphous surface scattering. This lower bound reflects heat conduction in graphene under realistic device conditions and provides a reference for fundamental phonon transport studies and the integration of graphene into thermal management applications in electronic devices and chips.

papers.title: Learning and Generating Time Trajectories of Multidimensional Stochastic Processes
papers.abstract: We present a multidimensional statistics-informed neural network (SINN) framework for learning and generating trajectories of multicomponent stochastic processes. SINN is built upon a deterministic recurrent neural network that takes streams of white-noise sequences as input and generates ensembles of stochastic trajectories whose statistical properties match those of the underlying stochastic dynamics. While SINN has been demonstrated for various one-dimensional non-Markovian processes, extending it to multidimensional processes is essential for real-world applications. Here, we present key developments toward this goal. First, because direct estimation of multivariate probability density functions (PDFs) becomes computationally challenging with increasing dimension, we represent joint-distribution information using collections of one-dimensional PDFs constructed from linear combinations of the process components. Second, to accommodate the larger set of statistical objectives required to characterize multidimensional processes, we adopt a self-adaptive loss-balancing strategy that dynamically weights the components of the total loss function. Third, we introduce a reference-normalized validation framework that interprets statistical discrepancies relative to the finite-sample variability between independent target ensembles. We also investigate the role of the input white-noise dimension in SINN performance. We evaluate the proposed approach using a Langevin benchmark based on two coupled Duffing oscillators and further demonstrate its applicability to the Langevin dynamics of the Fermi-Pasta-Ulam chain and kinetic Monte Carlo simulations of a lattice Lotka-Volterra model. Our results demonstrate that the multidimensional SINN framework provides a practical approach for modeling multidimensional stochastic dynamics.

papers.title: A Tumour-Aware Multimodal Framework for Explainable Prediction of IDH Mutation in Gliomas from Multi-Sequence MRI
papers.abstract: Accurate prediction of isocitrate dehydrogenase (IDH) mutation status is essential for glioma diagnosis, prognosis, and treatment planning. Although recent deep learning approaches have demonstrated promising performance, many rely on whole-brain feature extraction and provide limited interpretability. This study proposes a tumour-aware multimodal framework for explainable, non-invasive prediction of IDH mutation status from multiparametric magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). The proposed framework integrates four MRI sequences (T1, T1CE, T2, and FLAIR), tumour subregion segmentation, quantitative radiomic descriptors, and clinical information within a unified deep learning architecture. An ablation study was conducted to evaluate the contribution of tumour-aware learning, radiomic features, and clinical variables. Model performance was assessed using multiple complementary evaluation metrics, including accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, balanced accuracy, receiver operating characteristic analysis, confusion matrix evaluation, and Grad-CAM visualisation. Experimental results demonstrated that the proposed multimodal framework consistently outperformed the baseline MRI-only model, with the Clinical Fusion model achieving the strongest overall predictive performance. The integration of tumour-aware learning, radiomic descriptors, and clinical information progressively improved classification performance, while Grad-CAM visualisations indicated that the model predominantly focused on biologically relevant tumour regions. These findings suggest that tumour-aware multimodal feature integration enables accurate, interpretable, and non-invasive molecular profiling of gliomas and provides a promising foundation for future clinical decision support in precision neuro-oncology.

papers.title: DesignSpecs: A DESIGN.md Dataset of Visual Design Specifications for AI Agents
papers.abstract: While AI agents increasingly generate and modify user interfaces, they rarely rely on a visual design specification for a certain project. The DESIGN$.$md format, which originated from Google's AI design tool Stitch and which was open-sourced in April 2026, addresses this gap by describing a visual identity through design tokens (such as named colors, text styles) and Markdown prose. To our knowledge, no large-scale research dataset of such design specification files exists. We present DesignSpecs, a dataset of 36,906 DESIGN$.$md files from 15,794 public, non-fork GitHub repositories, representing 17,240 unique file contents. We collected 613,207 files named DESIGN$.$md in October 2026. Because the same file name also denotes architectural plans and other design documents, we filtered those with YAML front matter, a design-system name, at least one recognized design token, and zero errors under the official linter. Our JSON Lines dataset provides file-level and deduplicated views of the original Markdown, links files to repositories, paths, and commits, and is released with related scripts. We outline research opportunities on visual design knowledge and design-aware AI agents. Dataset is available at: https://huggingface.co/datasets/Jl-wei/DesignSpecs

papers.title: Online Carbon-Aware Power Flexibility Quantification of Distributed Data Centers
papers.abstract: Geographically distributed data centers (DCs) can provide spatio-temporal power flexibility to electric grids through the coordinated management of computing resources and energy. Beyond their energy consumption, the carbon footprints of DCs are non-negligible, which constrain the power flexibility that DCs can offer to the power grid. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a carbon-aware power flexibility quantification framework for DCs. We first develop an optimization model that characterizes DC power flexibility in a grid-usable form, namely the Cartesian product of adjustable power demand intervals across time slots. An online algorithm based on Lyapunov optimization is then designed to solve the flexibility quantification model in real time under uncertain workload arrivals and fluctuating grid carbon intensity. Furthermore, an integrated disaggregation and feedback mechanism is devised to translate the power system operator's dispatch commands into real-time DC operating decisions and to capture their impact on future DC flexibility. Several desirable properties of the proposed model and method are proven, including disaggregation feasibility, bounded workload processing delays, and a bounded suboptimality gap. Numerical simulations demonstrate that our approach effectively unlocks DC power flexibility while satisfying carbon emission constraints, outperforming baseline algorithms.

papers.title: GIC model selection for high-dimensional CCA
papers.abstract: Canonical correlation analysis (CCA) is a widely used statistical tool for exploring the dependence structure between two sets of variables. An important issue in CCA is determining the rank. Among information-based criteria for rank selection, the Akaike information criterion (AIC) and the Bayesian information criterion (BIC) are two commonly used approaches. Both rely on the number of free parameters to quantify model complexity, which may not adequately account for the underlying dependence structure when the assumed model is misspecified. As a result, AIC and BIC may exhibit unsatisfactory performance, particularly when the remaining canonical correlations do not follow the assumed low-dimensional structure. To alleviate this difficulty, we adopt the idea of the generalized information criterion (GIC) to develop a data-adaptive measure of model complexity for CCA rank selection. The proposed complexity measure incorporates the magnitudes of the sample canonical correlations, thereby accounting for the spectral structure of the data and improving robustness to model misspecification. We investigate the asymptotic properties of the proposed GIC under a high-dimensional setting in which the sample size and both variable dimensions grow proportionally. Our theoretical analysis aims to characterize the conditions under which GIC can distinguish signal canonical correlations from noise and achieve more reliable rank selection than conventional information criteria.

papers.title: Cubic local observability of Gaussian-blind sources in thermal $φ^4_2$ fields
papers.abstract: We study external sources that are invisible to a spatially local observation in a massive Gaussian thermal field on a circle. A quadratic-reference calibration removes the first-order thermal mass-shift signal. For the resulting quartic model we prove a cutoff-independent, source-uniform $C^1$ expansion of local Wick cubic means. Its leading operator has the time-integrated cube of the thermal covariance as its kernel. A positive bilateral Laplace representation proves injectivity on the entire external source space, while analyticity gives exponential singular-value upper bounds. The expansion yields local Araki relative-entropy lower bounds on every fixed finite-dimensional source space, and a uniform separation theorem at every prescribed Sobolev resolution. Under an additional interval-length condition, a reflection-positivity identity yields an explicit, nonoptimal double-logarithmic conditional stability bound for this specific thermal kernel. Continuum probability estimates and the integrability assumptions of the Feynman--Kac--Nelson construction are verified in Section~3.

papers.title: Searching for signatures of criticality in heavy-ion collisions using two-pion correlation functions
papers.abstract: We study possible signatures of the existence of a Quantum Chromodynamics (QCD) critical end-point in low-energy relativistic heavy-ion collisions using two-pion femtoscopy. We simulate central $^{209}\mathrm{Bi}+^{209}\mathrm{Bi}$ collisions at center-of-mass energies ranging from $\sqrt{s_{NN}}=5.8$ to 11 GeV using the EPOS 4.0.3 framework, incorporating an equation of state that explicitly includes a critical end-point and is compatible with lattice QCD results at small baryon chemical potentials. We analyze the pion pair-distance distribution and the corresponding two-pion correlation function by fitting them with Lévy distributions in configuration and momentum spaces, respectively. We find a weak dependence of the source parameters on the collision energy below $\sqrt{s_{NN}}=9.2$ GeV, followed by a change in trend at higher energies, particularly in the intercept parameter $λ$. This behavior may be associated with a decreasing fraction of pions coming from the core and an increasing contribution from long-lived resonance decays. Within the present analysis, we do not identify an unambiguous signal attributable to the critical end-point. A comparison with simulations employing different equation of state parameters to vary the strength of the critical point, as well as with simulations without a critical end-point, is necessary to establish the sensitivity of these observables to critical phenomena.

papers.title: Observation of $^{71}$Cr and expanded cross-section measurements and analysis of $^{82}$Se fragmentation
papers.abstract: Production cross sections for neutron-rich nuclei from the fragmentation of $^{82}$Se were measured, including the previously unobserved isotope $^{71}$Cr. Particle identification of the mass number ($A$), atomic number ($Z$), and ionic charge state ($q$) was performed event-by-event using measurements of energy loss, time of flight, magnetic rigidity, and total kinetic energy. These measurements, combined with previous $^{82}$Se fragmentation data, were analyzed using an abrasion-ablation formalism and the recently developed $ΔBE$ systematics. Model dependence in both approaches was quantified through a Bayesian-inspired model averaging procedure based on eleven nuclear mass models. The $ΔBE$ systematics provide a simple means of incorporating nuclear structure information into production-rate predictions, while the abrasion-ablation analysis provides insight into the reaction mechanisms governing the production of neutron-rich nuclei. The production cross section predictions of these two approaches are in agreement for nuclei predicted to be well-bound by the mass models. Discrepancies between the two frameworks are large for nuclei near $N=48$, corresponding to pure-$Z$ removal. The agreement of $ΔBE_{\mathrm{sys}}$ with the experimental data and the under-prediction of the AA calculations point to a potentially incomplete description of the reaction mechanism governing the production of these isotopes. The first observation of $^{71}$Cr provides an out-of-sample test of the predictive capability of the $ΔBE$ systematics: a cross section of $1.94\times 10^{-13}$ mb, predicted using the HFB-22 mass table and $ΔBE_{\mathrm{sys}}$ coefficients determined before the observation of $^{71}$Cr, is consistent with the measured value reported here: $2.20^{+2.10}_{-0.75}\times10^{-13}$ mb.

papers.title: The non-stationary $\widehat{\mathfrak{gl}}_N$ affine Laumon function and its difference equation
papers.abstract: We present an explicit $q$-Givental type formula for the $\widehat{\mathfrak{gl}}_N$ non-stationary affine relativistic Toda or affine Laumon function introduced by Shiraishi. We prove the conjecture of [J. Shiraishi, Affine screening operators, affine Laumon spaces and conjectures concerning non-stationary Ruijsenaars functions. J. of Int. Systems, 4 (2019)], that this function obeys a non-stationary difference equation involving an operator $\widehat{\mathcal T}$, which represents a quiver automorphism (Dehn twist) of the quantum cluster algebra of the affine $A_{N-1}^{(1)}$ Q-system.

papers.title: Ego2Flow: Benchmarking the Traffic-System Impact of Autonomous Driving on Maps Distilled from Real-World Roads
papers.abstract: End-to-end autonomous driving is predominantly evaluated through ego-vehicle safety and task completion. Its deployment in urban traffic, however, creates sustained interactions among vehicles whose collective effects remain insufficiently evaluated. We introduce Ego2Flow, a closed-loop benchmark for assessing the traffic-system impact of autonomous driving on maps distilled from real-world cities. To construct realistic 3D urban environments for sustained closed-loop traffic simulation, we develop an agent-guided map distillation framework that integrates real-world maps and observations with complementary geographic information. Through an iterative feedback mechanism and a traffic information graph that jointly guide scene generation, the framework preserves lane topology, critical road geometry and decision-relevant visual conditions while simplifying nonessential details and completing unobserved regions. Using our proposed framework, we generate and publicly release six CARLA maps from the Argoverse 2 dataset, covering the corresponding real-world regions and enabling paired comparisons of driving behavior under real and simulated observations. On these maps, Ego2Flow evaluates how autonomous driving policies affect traffic efficiency, safety, stability and energy consumption across diverse road structures. Compared with existing construction methods, our framework achieves the lowest average displacement error between planning outputs from paired real and simulated observations. We further benchmark representative driving policies to characterize their system-level impact on urban traffic. Project Page: https://github.com/Fisher-007/Ego2Flow.

papers.title: Self-Consistent Subtracted Second Quasiparticle Random-Phase Approximation for Dipole Responses in Neutron-Rich Oxygen Isotopes
papers.abstract: Describing the nuclear dipole response in open-shell nuclei across wide energy scales, from low-lying states below the neutron separation energy to giant resonances near 30MeV, within a single microscopic framework is a long-standing open problem. Here we establish, for the first time, a self-consistent subtracted second quasiparticle random-phase approximation (SSQRPA) that simultaneously incorporates pairing correlations (HF+BCS), explicit two-quasiparticle (2qp) and four-quasiparticle (4qp) configurations in a large model space, the full forward- and backward-going QRPA structure, and a subtraction procedure to eliminate double counting and ensure stability. No existing framework unifies all of these ingredients in the quasiparticle basis. We apply SSQRPA to the dipole excitations of neutron-rich oxygen isotopes $^{18,20,22}$O, where the standard QRPA fails to simultaneously account for high-energy giant dipole resonance (GDR) states near 22--25MeV, medium-energy GDR states in the 10--18MeV region, and isolated low-lying $1^-$ states below the neutron separation energy. In SSQRPA, the dominant isovector (IV) GDR strength shifts downward by approximately 4MeV into the experimentally observed medium-energy region, while the compressional isoscalar (IS) GDR strength remains concentrated at higher energies, in qualitative agreement with the observed electromagnetic dissociation cross sections. For the low-lying states, the root-mean-square deviation from experiment is reduced from 5.31MeV (QRPA) to 0.35MeV (SSQRPA) in $^{18}$O, and from 4.07MeV to 0.74MeV in $^{20}$O, demonstrating that 4qp correlations are essential for a simultaneous description of dipole excitations over a wide range of excitation energies. The SSQRPA provides a powerful and general framework for future microscopic studies of collective excitations in open-shell nuclei across the nuclear mass table.

papers.title: Federated Soft Poly-Level Learning Over a Distributed Network with Guaranteed Convergence
papers.abstract: Multi-level learning/optimization, e.g., bilevel optimization, has been recognized for its versatile applicability across a broad array of domains, spanning from signal processing to machine learning. However, most existing works focus on bilevel and trilevel optimization. In contrast, multi-level optimization problems involving four or more hierarchical levels, which we term poly-level learning (PLL) problems, remain largely unexplored.In addition, in practical PLL, data may be distributed across multiple nodes over a distributed network. Nevertheless, extant studies on PLL predominantly focus on the non-federated setting, necessitating the collection of data to central servers and thereby posing potential privacy risks. To this end, we propose a Federated Poly-Level Learning (FPLL) framework over a distributed network to tackle the PLL problems with soft constraints in a federated manner. FPLL hinges on a novel non-linear cut, i.e., $L$-cut, for the level-wise relaxation to the PLL problems. Additionally, the proposed federated algorithm is designed with adjustable parameters that allow for a flexible trade-off between its computational complexity and performance efficiency, enabling users to tune it according to specific application requirements. We also carry out non-asymptotic analysis to derive the iteration complexity for the proposed FPLL to achieve the $ε$-Pareto stationary point. Extensive experiments have been undertaken to elucidate the superior efficacy of the proposed method.

papers.title: uhd-rfsoc: Bringing Off-the-Shelf RFSoC Boards to Unmodified UHD Applications
papers.abstract: Next-generation wireless research relies on software-defined radios (SDRs) with more channels and larger bandwidth. The USRP family is one of the most widely used SDR platforms, and much of the wireless software ecosystem is built on top of the USRP hardware driver (UHD). However, each USRP model comes with a fixed channel count, bandwidth, and streaming capability. Off-the-shelf radio frequency system-on-chip (RFSoC) boards, on the other hand, integrate up to 16 analog-to-digital converters (ADCs) and 16 digital-to-analog converters (DACs) operating at several gigasamples per second (GS/s), but existing UHD applications cannot directly use them. We present uhd-rfsoc, an open-source FPGA design and host software stack that turns these boards, including the 16-channel ZCU216 and the RFSoC 4x2, into standard UHD devices without modifying UHD. Through standard UHD calls, applications can configure the carrier frequency, channel count, the per-channel I/Q sample rate, and the wire format. uhd-rfsoc combines timestamped, flow-controlled sample transport in the FPGA with data plane development kit (DPDK) packet processing and vectorized sample conversion on x86 and Arm hosts. The built bitstreams for a number of RFSoC board configurations with varying RF data converter rates, channel counts, I/Q sample rates, and wire formats all successfully pass UHD's built-in streaming benchmarks. We further demonstrate compatibility with unmodified GNU Radio flowgraphs, a custom GPU-accelerated transceiver digital signal processing pipeline, as well as the OCUDU and Duranta 5G radio access network stacks using both software and commodity user equipment.

papers.title: Anyon Proliferation at Self-Triality: From a Lattice Model to Adjoint QCD$_3$
papers.abstract: We study how competitive proliferation among three types of anyons in a self-trial $\mathbb{Z}_2\times\mathbb{Z}_2$ gauge theory can drive symmetry breaking while preserving part of the topological order. We construct a deformation of the honeycomb color code, a spin model rooted in quantum error correction, with an $S_3$ symmetry that permutes the competing anyons, together with time-reversal and fermionic $\mathbb{Z}_2^{(1)}$ one-form symmetries. We propose two dual continuum descriptions of this transition. The bosonic description is a $\mathrm{PSU}(3)_3\times\mathrm{Spin}(8)_{-1}$ Chern-Simons-Higgs theory with a real Higgs field in the $(\mathbf{8}_{\mathrm{adj}},\mathbf{8}_v)$ representation. Fermion-boson duality gives a particularly simple fermionic dual: $\mathrm{PSU}(3)_{3/2}$ QCD$_3$ with a single adjoint Majorana fermion and gauged fermion parity. Both descriptions match the lattice model's unitary symmetries and proposed phase diagram, connecting double-toric-code order to a symmetry-broken phase with residual toric-code order. The transition is described by Higgs condensation and by a Majorana mass changing sign, respectively. The continuum theories are proposed to recover lattice time reversal at criticality. This connection to adjoint QCD$_3$ points to a possible continuous $S_3$-breaking transition from competing anyons, in contrast to the conventional first-order three-state Potts transition from competing local order parameters.

papers.title: Axion quintessence with a negative cosmological constant: Bayesian constraints from current cosmological data
papers.abstract: We constrain canonical axion quintessence with a negative cosmological constant using DES Year 5 supernovae, DESI DR2 BAO, compressed CMB information, and geometry-corrected Gold-2017 growth data. We solve the background and linear-growth equations and sample with PolyChord. Our joint prior is logarithmic in the decay constant over $0.005\leq f/M_{\rm Pl}\leq10$ and uniform in the initial angle $θ_i=φ_i/f\in[0,π]$, conditioned on $π-θ_i\geq H_{\rm inf}/(2πf)$ with $H_{\rm inf}=10^{13}$ GeV and reduced Planck mass $M_{\rm Pl}$. The broad-prior model favors recent thawing, with median $w_{{\rm DE},0}=-0.865^{+0.068}_{-0.053}$, $m_φ\in[0.91,4.39]\times10^{-33}$ eV, and $f/M_{\rm Pl}\in[0.589,4.899]$ (central 68\% credible intervals). Bayes factors relative to flat $Λ$CDM are 0.70 and 30.1 for the normalized fluctuation-conditioned prior (Convention I) and its further conditioning on numerical acceptance (Convention II). Restricting $f\leq M_{\rm Pl}$ gives $f/M_{\rm Pl}\in[0.262,0.822]$ at 68\% credibility and Bayes factors 0.233 and 32.4. Relative to the zero-vacuum axion model, the broad-prior Bayes factors are 0.620 and 1.65, providing no compelling evidence for a negative cosmological constant. Local likelihood optimization gives an Akaike information criterion difference $Δ{\rm AIC}\simeq-10.87$ for the zero-vacuum model relative to flat $Λ$CDM. For this model, assuming that the instanton generating $m_φ^2f^2=Λ_{\rm UV}^4e^{-S_{\rm inst}}$ satisfies the axionic Weak Gravity Conjecture, the one-sided 95\% posterior lower limit on the minimum compatible coefficient $c_{\min}$ rises from 37 to 55 as the ultraviolet scale $Λ_{\rm UV}$ increases from $10^{-10}M_{\rm Pl}$ to $M_{\rm Pl}$, in tension with an order-one coefficient under these assumptions.

papers.title: Towards High-Performance Multimodal Discovery: Evaluating Retrieval Efficacy and Operational Scalability in Digital Libraries
papers.abstract: Large-scale digital repositories with million plus digitized volumes serve as vital engines for scientific and scholarly discovery. However, as collections grow, finding specific research or educational material remains a significant challenge. This difficulty is compounded by the multimodal nature of texts, that is, texts which combine dense narrative content with essential illustrative charts, annotated diagrams, and complex layouts. Historically, discovery has been supported by full-text search indexes implemented as inverted indexes (e.g., Lucene or Solr). While these systems scale well for textual strings, they are fundamentally "blind" to the semantic nuance of visual information. We explore the benefit of discovery through texts that have been converted to numerical vectors. By representing page images as numerical vectors rather than OCR-extracted text, and doing so for both text and images on a page, we capture both textual and visual semantics while mitigating reverse engineering and copyright infringement concerns. The primary contribution of this research is an evaluation of the multimodal retrieval landscape, encompassing both semantic precision and architectural scalability. Our findings demonstrate that integrating visual and textual features significantly enhances the discovery of relevant material, particularly in domains where diagrammatic content is essential for conceptual understanding. We assess retrieval efficacy, demonstrating that the system achieves sub-linear scalability. Our findings suggest that an optimized vector database configuration is the critical factor in transforming VLM-based embeddings into a production-ready, library-scale discovery solution.

papers.title: Proximal Adam algorithm for nonsmooth composite optimization and linear convergence under proximal PL geometry
papers.abstract: We analyze Adam-type methods for nonsmooth composite optimization problems $\min_xΦ(x)=f(x)+h(x)$, where $f$ is smooth and $h$ is convex, proper, and lower semicontinuous. The nonsmooth term is treated by a metric-weighted proximal map, while the smooth term is preconditioned by the Adam second-moment matrix. We prove a composite descent lemma whose constants depend explicitly on the spectral bounds of the adaptive metric and a residual--step equivalence that converts proximal step decay into subgradient stationarity. These yield an $O(1/N)$ bound on the minimum proximal stationarity residual for the deterministic proximal normalized gradient method without convexity of $f$, and the same $O(1/N)$ rate for proximal Adam under quantitative momentum-alignment and residual-coherence conditions together with a metric-compatibility condition. By estimating the momentum error directly, the same $O(1/N)$ rate is also obtained without the momentum-alignment and residual-coherence assumptions. When the composite objective satisfies a proximal Polyak--Łojasiewicz inequality, both algorithms and the relaxed proximal Adam scheme converge linearly with explicit contraction factors. Numerical experiments on a diagonal Lasso problem, two-dimensional image TV denoising, and two-dimensional elastic parameter identification illustrate the predicted stationarity and linear rates.

papers.title: A Spectral Framework for Universal Proxy Regularization in Model Merging
papers.abstract: Model merging constructs multi-task models without expensive joint training but often suffers from parameter interference. Some solutions mitigate this by constraining finetuning using data from the other tasks to be merged, violating the core independence and privacy assumption of model merging. Recent work offers preliminary empirical evidence that a universal, task-agnostic proxy distribution can substitute for such data, but leaves open when and why it suffices. To this end, we propose a \textit{Spectral Framework for Universal Proxy Regularization}, which characterizes the relationship between a proxy distribution and the distribution of other tasks to be merged through spectral coverage ($α$) and leakage ($β$). Based on the framework, we derive a unified parameter interference bound: smaller $(α, β)$ provably yields lower parameter interference through better spectral alignment. To exploit such a proxy, we augment the training objective with a proxy regularizer. Evaluating this regularizer during fine-tuning requires a concrete mechanism. We study three instantiations, including (J) an exact evaluation via Jacobian-vector products, (F) a frozen curvature approximation using the Fisher information matrix, and (O) an output-drift formulation that constrains the model's functional deviation on the proxy directly. We prove that all three coincide under the NTK linearization, where existing analyses of such regularizers stop, and go further to characterize standard non-linear fine-tuning, bounding how far each instantiation departs from its linearized reference and obtain a three-way hierarchy, zero for (J), proxy-independent for (F), and proxy-quality-scaling for (O). Empirical validation on the commonly used vision-language model CLIP confirms these theoretical predictions.

papers.title: Dopant-vacancy complexes as single-photon-emitter candidates in monolayer silicon carbide: radiative and nonradiative decay
papers.abstract: Solid-state color centers have emerged as promising single-photon sources (SPSs). In particular, color centers in two-dimensional (2D) materials combine high photon brightness with scalable fabrication and ease of integration, offering a versatile platform for quantum information technologies. Realizing high-efficiency SPSs, however, requires strong radiative emission and negligible nonradiative decay. Using first-principles calculations, we assess radiative and nonradiative decay in dopant-vacancy complexes XSiVC (X = N, O, P, and S) in monolayer silicon carbide. All four defects exhibit stable neutral charge states and inter-defect optical transitions. Among them, PSiVC emerges as the leading single-photon-emitter candidate, combining rapid radiative decay with negligible nonradiative decay and a near-unity quantum yield within the modeled channels. By contrast, multiphonon decay limits the quantum yield of NSiVC despite its high Debye-Waller factor. Hyperfine tensors provide characteristic signatures for identifying the spin-active centers. Beyond identifying promising candidates, these results establish a joint radiative-nonradiative screening strategy and provide theoretical guidance for the rational design of color centers as solid-state SPSs.

papers.title: ERA: Error-Resistant Autonomous Object Navigation with Predicted Depth
papers.abstract: Depth and 3D foundation models can predict geometry from RGB images, allowing zero-shot object navigation without a depth sensor. However, when predicted depth is mapped as if it came from a sensor, view-dependent errors accumulate in the map, remove exploration goals, and end the search before the agent can observe and correct them. We propose ERA, a training-free object navigation system that replaces the depth sensor with depth predicted from RGB images and poses. ERA follows a paradigm we call Move with Error: movement provides new views that correct map errors, and the corrected map enables further movement. It realizes this paradigm with revisable occupancy and with exploration from reachable viewpoints, which continues the search when no frontier remains, and verifies the target across views before stopping. On three benchmarks, ERA achieves state-of-the-art performance among training-free methods without depth sensors. Its map and exploration components also raise VLFM's success from 10.8% to 61.7% under the same predicted depth. We further deploy ERA on a real robot.

papers.title: Ultrafast Imaging Reveals Energy Transport Anisotropy Grows from Bulk to Monolayer Black Phosphorus
papers.abstract: Black phosphorus is an emerging low-dimensional semiconductor whose tunable band gap, high carrier mobility, and anisotropic transport make it attractive for directional energy transport in electronics and thermoelectrics. Using ultrafast stroboscopic optical scattering microscopy (stroboSCAT), we image spatiotemporal evolution of energy carriers with picosecond resolution, simultaneously resolving heat and charge transport in bulk black phosphorus and exciton transport in the monolayer. The in-plane armchair:zigzag anisotropy increases from 5.3:1 in the bulk to 6.7:1 in the monolayer, driven by enhanced armchair exciton diffusivity (45.5 cm$^2$/s) relative to bulk armchair charge carriers (16.5 cm$^2$/s). The monolayer anisotropy is smaller than the calculated exciton dispersion alone would suggest, which first-principles calculations attribute to preferential exciton-phonon scattering to large momenta along the zigzag direction. These directly measured, layer-resolved diffusivities identify armchair-aligned monolayers as the optimal geometry for directional transport and show that transport anisotropy cannot be inferred from band dispersion alone.

papers.title: Rigidity for pivotal braided r-categories of moderate growth and applications to vertex operator algebras
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal{C}$ be an abelian pivotal braided r-category with simple unit object $\mathbf{1}$ over any field. We present a ChatGPT-generated proof, prompted by Bin Gui, that any object $X$ in $\mathcal{C}$ of moderate growth, in the sense that $\dim\mathrm{End}(X^{\otimes n})<n!$ for some $n\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 1}$, is rigid. The proof crucially uses ideas from the recent proof of Etingof and Penneys that $X$ is rigid if it is also non-negligible, that is, $X\otimes Y$ contains $\mathbf{1}$ as a direct summand for some object $Y$. In the present paper, the non-negligible assumption is removed using a rigidity criterion developed previously by the author for use in non-semisimple categories. We also present a variant result (found without further AI assistance) that $X$ is also rigid if $\dim\mathrm{Hom}((DX)^{\otimes n}\otimes X^{\otimes n},\mathbf{1})<n!$ for some $n\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 1}$, where $D$ is the Grothendieck-Verdier duality functor of $\mathcal{C}$. Using this variant, we show that if $V$ is a simple self-contragredient vertex operator algebra such that the category $\mathcal{C}^1_V$ of $C_1$-cofinite grading-restricted generalized $V$-modules is closed under contragredient modules, then $\mathcal{C}^1_V$ is a locally finite $\mathbb{C}$-linear abelian rigid braided ribbon category. We also show that if $V$ is a simple $\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}$-graded self-contragredient $C_2$-cofinite vertex operator algebra, then the category of all grading-restricted generalized $V$-modules is a (not necessarily semisimple) modular tensor category.

papers.title: HarmonyText: Harmonious Scene Text Editing via Reverse-to-Refined Pair Synthesis and Region-Decoupled Frequency Learning
papers.abstract: Natural language-guided, mask-free scene text editing aims to modify text in real-world images using only textual instructions, yet remains challenged by unreliable pseudo-GT supervision, over-smoothed text generation, and the absence of GT-free evaluation. Existing methods often rely on imperfect pseudo-targets with background discrepancies, while standard MSE-based velocity regression tends to suppress high-frequency details, leading to blurred text boundaries and weakened local textures. To address these issues, we propose HarmonyText, a mask-free scene text editing framework with region- and frequency-aware supervision. HarmonyText introduces Region-Decoupling Optimization (RDO), which aligns edited text regions with pseudo-targets while anchoring preserved regions to the source image, and Cascaded High-Frequency Texture Guidance (CHFTG), which applies cascaded wavelet-domain constraints to preserve sharp boundaries and fine-grained textures of textual content. We further propose Reverse-to-Refined Pair Synthesis (RePair) to construct STE25K, a high-quality 25K paired dataset, and introduce a GT-free evaluation protocol with Color Distribution Divergence and a Harmony Assessment Model. Extensive experiments show that HarmonyText outperforms existing methods in text editing accuracy, background fidelity, color consistency, and perceptual harmony.

papers.title: Global generation of coinvariant vector bundles on $\overline{\mathrm{M}}_{0,n}$
papers.abstract: Using fusion closed-ness and strong generation properties, we identify collections of modules over vertex operator algebras (VOAs) whose induced vector bundles of coinvariants on the moduli space $\overline{\mathrm M}_{0,n}$ of stable $n$-pointed curves of genus zero are globally generated. These results specialize to \cite{Fak12} for affine VOAs at positive integer levels, and of \cite{DG23} for strongly rational VOAs that are generated in degree 1. To illustrate the results, and to show that fusion-closedness is essential, we give numerous examples, including Lattice VOAs, Simple Current Extensions of Affine VOAs, and various tensor products.

papers.title: Logically Consistent Accurate Forecasts
papers.abstract: Agentic forecasting systems based on large language models (LLMs) are now competitive with expert human forecasters, but these systems still suffer from a critical limitation: the inability to produce forecasts that are logically consistent. For example, forecasts for related events often fail to satisfy the axioms of probability, which in turn implies that related forecasts cannot simultaneously be correct and undermines their utility for decision makers. Enforcing consistency is not trivial -- naive approaches (e.g., projection onto the set of consistent forecasts) can degrade accuracy. We argue that the key to overcoming the apparent tradeoff between consistency and accuracy lies in the reasoning which supports each forecast. We finetune a supervisory language model that leverages this reasoning to jointly reconcile inconsistencies while improving the accuracy of related forecasts. On ForecastBench, our method improves the Brier score of a retrieval-augmented GPT-5.1 forecaster by 9.3% while reducing measures of structural inconsistency by 82-90%. We interrogate our method via a comprehensive series of baselines and ablations, and find that no alternative method matches our gains in consistency and accuracy simultaneously.

papers.title: High-probability convergence of adaptive, proximal, and clipped Adam-type methods for nonconvex stochastic optimization
papers.abstract: This paper develops a unified high-probability analysis of adaptive, proximal, and clipped first-order methods for nonconvex stochastic optimization. For a smooth objective whose stochastic gradient error has sub-Gaussian norm, the normalized adaptive gradient method attains the standard stochastic nonconvex complexity of the square root of the number of iterations, with an additional logarithmic dependence on the inverse confidence level that is inversely proportional to the number of iterations. The proof uses an adaptive descent decomposition together with Freedman and Bernstein concentration inequalities. The same guarantee is established for the full adaptive moment method under an explicit momentum-alignment condition. The analysis is extended to projected and proximal updates through a stationarity measure based on the subdifferential distance, to objectives satisfying the Polyak-Lojasiewicz condition, and to heavy-tailed noise through truncation. The framework is applied to stochastic inverse problems in elasticity, and numerical experiments illustrate the theoretical scaling and the practical behavior of the methods.

papers.title: An LLM-assisted theoretical model for aeroengine installation noise scattering
papers.abstract: A theoretical model is developed for the canonical problem of aeroengine fan noise impinging on, and scattering from, a nearby semi-infinite rigid plate. The model chains two Wiener--Hopf problems in different coordinate systems. The first stage solves the duct-radiation problem analytically in axisymmetric cylindrical coordinates. The second stage expands the field incident on the plate into a double angular spectrum of plane waves: the axial spectrum is inherited from the first stage, while the spanwise spectrum is generated by a Weyl--Sommerfeld expansion of the cylindrical harmonics. Each spectral component is then scattered by the plate. The mathematical crux is the coordinate transformation between the axisymmetric duct frame and the Cartesian plate frame. The core physical insight--that the Weyl--Sommerfeld identity provides an exact spectral bridge between these systems--originates entirely with the authors. The heavy algebra of translating between the two spectral representations, together with the associated numerical verification, was carried out with the assistance of a large language model (LLM), under strict human oversight and independent numerical cross-checking. This division of labour enables the LLM to handle tedious symbolic manipulation without compromising rigour. Results are presented for spinning modes radiating from a cylindrical duct with a subsonic jet into a quiescent ambient. The case study demonstrates that, under systematic verification, LLMs can accelerate tedious algebra in theoretical fluid mechanics, contributing a concrete empirical example to the broader discussion on AI's role in theoretical research.

papers.title: Super-Analysis for Aggressive yet Scalable Compiler Optimization
papers.abstract: Aggressive compiler optimization today occupies two distant extremes. Conventional optimizers run in milliseconds but reason through ad-hoc heuristics that miss opportunities; superoptimizers synthesize faster code but take hours, confining them to small kernels and offline use. We introduce solver-based super-analysis, a middle ground that uses expensive SMT-based analysis while transformations remain conventional, avoiding program synthesis entirely. The key argument for super-analysis is that conventional compilers have rich transformation rules, but proving them to be safe requires complex reasoning: proving a safety check dead often needs facts from three independent LLVM analyses simultaneously, a conjunctive entailment problem suited to an SMT solver, not to any single dataflow pass. We instantiate super-analysis in ODeSSy, an LLVM pass that proves sanitizer traps and native-language safety checks unreachable and removes them. One mechanism serves four frontend languages and yields speedups in each, including a 3.78x speedup for a GEMM implemented in Julia. A further solver-based optimization, guard synthesis, handles checks that are not dead for every input: the solver synthesizes a cheap invariant safety guard under which a fast check-free loop is cloned, speeding up a Swift Base64 encoder by 1.44x and a Julia LZ77 compressor by 4.01x. Compared with Souper, the synthesizing superoptimizer for LLVM, ODeSSy removes more safety checks in significantly less time, making it viable as an online compiler pass.

papers.title: Fast forward-and-backward creation of non-equilibrium Gibbs state in driven dissipative quantum systems
papers.abstract: We present the fast-forward (FF) approach to adiabatic time evolution of an open dissipative quantum system within the framework of the Gorini-Kosaakowski-Sudarshan-Lindblad (GKSL) equation. Taking a harmonic oscillator (HO) and a quantum spin as prototype systems under a rapid change of the driving field and in contact with the heat reservoir, we reveal the protocol which creates the non-equilibrium Gibbs state. After preparing the Gibbs state under the fixed external field in advance, we begin to change adiabatically the field. To keep a quasi-adiabatic version of the Gibbs state as the solution of GKSL equation, we solve the inverse problem to obtain the non-adiabatic corrections both to Hamiltonian and to the dissipator. Then we apply the fast forward-and-backward (abbreviated as FF for convenience) time-rescaling, obtaining the FF variants of both Hamiltonian and detailed balance condition (DBC) among dissipative coefficients. The present scheme generates the time-periodic Gibbs state as if a limit-cycle solution of the innovated GKSL equation under the time-periodic driving field. Thanks to the FF variant of DBC, we see the energy conservation of power and heat current of the system, and reversibility of whole system including a reservoir. The requirement of positivity of the FF dissipative coefficients imposes a constraint on the speed of the FF driving. At low temperature, the upper speed limit of the FF periodic driving is found to be proportional to $\tildeβ^{-1/2}\exp(a\tildeβ)$ with $\tildeβ$ the scaled inverse temperature and $a$ the positive constant of $O(1)$.

papers.title: State-of-Charge Targets for Storage Participation in Two-Settlement Markets: Reliability, Price, and Compensation Impacts
papers.abstract: As energy storage assumes a larger role in electricity systems, market operation must coordinate its use across time to support reliability during periods of system stress. Minimum state-of-charge (SOC) targets provide a means of preserving energy for these periods, but their design shapes reliability, operating efficiency, and storage compensation. This paper evaluates alternative SOC target designs in a California-based day-ahead and real-time electricity market model. The comparison examines targets based on day-ahead schedules or rolling centralized dispatch, enforced at the individual-resource or system level, across seasons, stress conditions, and participant information settings. The results show that retaining more energy does not necessarily reduce load shedding: targets that restrict discharge can limit storage support during shortages. Under critical summer conditions, individual targets derived from rolling centralized dispatch reduce weekly load shedding by approximately 83--84\% relative to operation without targets. Lower RT clearing costs and average prices can coexist with higher storage compensation, reflecting the role of day-ahead positions and real-time deviations in determining settlement outcomes. These findings highlight the importance of coordinating energy retention with timely discharge and network deliverability when designing SOC requirements for storage participation in electricity markets.

papers.title: Counter-rotating Ionized and Neutral Gas in a Star-forming Elliptical Galaxy
papers.abstract: In early-type galaxies, gas that is kinematically misaligned with the stars generally rotates together across all gas phases, implying a single external origin. Using upgraded Giant Metrewave Radio Telescope (uGMRT) 21 cm imaging and SDSS-MaNGA spatially resolved spectroscopy, we studied MaNGA 10214-1902, a compact ($R_e = 0.78$ kpc), star-forming elliptical galaxy with stellar mass $\log M_*/M_{\odot} = 9.90$, in which the ionized gas counter-rotates with respect to the stars. It hosts $\log(M_{\rm HI}/M_{\odot}) = 9.65$ in a 45 kpc HI disk that co-rotates with the stars and has a central column-density depression. Inside this depression, the ionized gas ($r \lesssim 2$ kpc) rotates in the opposite sense to both the stars ($Δ{\rm PA} = 152^\circ \pm 20^\circ$) and the HI that surrounds it ($Δ{\rm PA} = 179^\circ \pm 10^\circ$). HI co-spatial with the ionized gas is not detected, so a fainter inner HI component with a different orientation cannot be ruled out. This central gas is star-forming in the [SII] and [OI] diagnostic diagrams and has EW(HI) $>6~\mathrm{\mathring{A}}$ at the center. The 1.4 GHz radio-continuum star formation rate agrees with the spectral energy distribution based value, showing no evidence of a dominant active galactic nucleus. The stellar population at the center is younger than the outskirts and has the lowest D$_{\rm n}$4000. These results are consistent with the acquisition of gas with opposite angular momentum into the center of a pre-existing HI disk that co-rotates with the stars, which can fuel the most recent central star formation.

papers.title: Vision-Language Models Reproduce a Human Mental-Extrapolation Bias in the Watanabe Illusion
papers.abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) are increasingly used for visual judgments, yet whether they share human perceptual biases, and where in the model such biases arise, is unclear. We addressed this with the Watanabe Illusion, a stimulus not previously studied quantitatively: an oblique segment inside a circle whose extension geometrically hits the topmost of 11 dots, yet human observers (n = 131) reported a dot near the middle of the column. Five VLMs (Qwen2.5-VL-32B and 7B, Claude Sonnet 4.6, GPT-5.5 Instant, Gemini 3.5 Flash), given the identical stimulus and wording, all deviated in the same direction. In the open-weight Qwen2.5-VL-32B, linear probes on the vision encoder recovered the line angle and the target dot six to eight times more accurately than its behavioral responses. A layer-wise logit lens showed that the correct answer dominates in the middle layers of the language model and is overwritten in late layers only under a visual-judgment frame. Naming the illusion, requesting suppression of prior knowledge, forcing a visual chain of thought, and 390 semantic preambles left the response center unchanged; only disclosing the correct answer moved it. VLMs may therefore carry human perceptual biases at the language-generation stage, where they resist declarative correction.

papers.title: Analysing Busy Beaver Machines (Or How to Find Ossified Ocelots)
papers.abstract: The busy beaver problem involves working with machines which can produce very large numbers, both for the output of certain Turing machines and for the number of steps taken to execute them. Given that these numbers can involve thousands of digits, it is crucial to have a means of proving properties of the relevant machines which allow manipulation of such large numbers. In this paper we introduce the notion of \textit{shape computations} as a means of isolating key properties that allow efficient execution of the relevant Turing machines based on verifiable properties of state transitions. In particular, this notion allows us to provide an analytical result which demonstrates the quadratic relationship between the size of the output and the number of steps required to generate it. We have also developed an initial implementation of our approach, and we provide empirical evaluation of it on a suite of 240 example machines.

papers.title: X-Strata: Separating Aneurysms and Overlapping Vessels into Layers from 2D X-ray Angiography
papers.abstract: An X-ray angiogram sums every structure along a ray into one pixel. When vessels cross an aneurysm, they obscure part of it and mix their contrast into its filling curve. We present X-Strata, a network that separates a cine angiogram into three layers: the complete aneurysm sac, the vessels in front of it, and the vessels behind it. Contrast timing indicates how much each layer contributes to a pixel, and parallax between two views indicates their order, which a single view cannot determine. X-Strata first estimates the layers and their contrast curves, then uses the second view to assign vessels to the front or back layer, and lifts all layers into 3D. It learns from layer labels projected from same-session 3D rotational angiography, but needs only 2D cine runs and their acquisition geometry at inference. On 220 held-out patients from three centers (122 external), two-view X-Strata ranks first among 14 baselines, including VGGT and C$^2$RV, in recovering the sac where vessels overlap it (Dice 0.693 internal, 0.641 external) and in ordering the layers (balanced accuracy 0.703, 0.659). Its order accuracy exceeds that of all 11 end-to-end baselines by at least 4.1 points internally and 3.3 externally (Holm-adjusted $p < 0.001$) and grows with view separation. Recovered 3D sac surfaces have a median Chamfer distance of 0.34 mm on the internal cohort. X-Strata may therefore provide layered aneurysm and vessel information, including 3D sac shape, for patients who undergo only 2D angiography.

papers.title: Minimaxity in Robust Nonparametric Regression: from Heavy-Tailed to Sub-Gaussian Assumptions
papers.abstract: We study nonparametric regression over star-shaped function classes under strong adversarial contamination. The clean (original) observations $(\tilde{X} _{i},\tilde{Y} _{i})_{i=1} ^{n}$ are i.i.d. and satisfy $\tilde{Y} _{i}=f ^{*}(\tilde{X} _{i})+ξ_{i}$, where $f ^{*}\in \mathcal{F}$, $\tilde{X}$ is distributed as $\mathbb{P} _{X}$, and the noise is conditionally centered. An adversary may inspect the clean sample and replace at most $\lfloor εn\rfloor$ observation pairs. We assume that $\mathcal{F}\subset L _{2}(\mathbb{P} _{X})$ is star-shaped with finite diameter $d$. Under a Bernstein-type moment condition on function increments and a bounded conditional second moment for the noise, we establish the matching lower and upper bounds of order $\left((η^{*}) ^{2} \vee ε\right)\wedge d ^{2}$, uniformly over admissible star-shaped function classes, therefore characterizing the minimax rate of estimation error, where \begin{equation*} η^{*}:=\sup\left\{η>0: nη^2\leq\log \mathcal M _{\mathcal{F}}^{\text{loc}}(η,c)\right\}. \end{equation*} Here $\log \mathcal{M} _{\mathcal{F}} ^{\text{loc}}(η,c)$ denotes the local metric entropy of $\mathcal{F}$ in $L _2(\mathbb{P} _{X})$, and $c$ is a sufficiently large constant. Under a uniform relative sub-Gaussian condition on function increments and noise, the lower bound is adjusted to $\left((η^{*})^{2}\vee ε^{2}\right)\wedge d ^{2}$ while the upper bound improves to $\left((η^{*})^{2}\vee ε^{2}\log ^{2}\left(\frac{e}{ε}\right)\right)\wedge d ^{2}$, yielding minimax optimality up to logarithmic factors.

papers.title: The Polyak-Łojasiewicz Paper: A 10-Year Retrospective
papers.abstract: In 2016, we wrote a paper introducing the phrase "Polyak-Lojasiewicz (PL) condition" for an old idea, unsure of how readers would react. The paper ultimately had a larger impact than we expected, and we are surprised and honoured to receive the 2026 PKDD ECML Test of Time Award. With 10 years of hindsight, this note offers an informal and candid retrospective on the PL condition. We take a look back at the origins of the paper, give an AI-assisted refined version of the main theorem, review criticisms of the work, and discuss a variety of related ideas and extensions.

papers.title: Complex Schrödinger Bridges
papers.abstract: Diffusion bridges have emerged as versatile frameworks for facilitating transformations between arbitrary data distributions. However, these approaches are hindered by an immense optimization space and its underlying high-order structures. This paper explores a variant of diffusion bridges for solving real-world problems in complex vector spaces governed by scaling and rotation laws, such as Hamiltonian structures. To address this, we introduce conformal optimal transport (COT), a complex-valued transportation framework designed for physical systems with geometric and dissipative dynamics under a geometric lifting. Building on this, we propose a new class of dynamical diffusion bridges, called complex Schrödinger bridges (CSBs), whose derived algorithms can handle diffusion-based tasks using a conformal geometric prior. For scalability, we propose image-to-image CSB (I$^2$CSB), a tractable diffusion-bridge technique with an analytic spiral posterior. Finally, we implement a physics-informed CSB algorithm within simulations of quantum electrodynamics, mimicking the logical behavior of quantum logic gates. Our extensive results validate the underlying theory while highlighting advantages of complex-valued diffusion.

papers.title: Evaluating the Robustness of PRNU Source-Camera Attribution to the Fingerprint-Copy Attack: An Open Toolkit with Triangle-Test Detection
papers.abstract: Photo-Response Non-Uniformity (PRNU) is the de facto standard trace for sensor-level source-camera attribution, and a high Peak-to-Correlation-Energy (PCE) between a questioned image and a camera reference fingerprint is routinely treated as strong evidence of common origin. The fingerprint-copy attack of Goljan, Fridrich and Chen (2011) shows that this signal can be forged: an adversary who estimates a target camera's fingerprint from that camera's publicly available images can inject a scaled copy of it into an unrelated photograph, producing a forgery that clears a PCE decision threshold despite never having been taken by the target device. We present prnucf, an open, auditable toolkit that pairs a reference implementation of the (additive) fingerprint-copy attack with the triangle-test detector and a cohort-calibrated decision procedure, so that practitioners can quantify how fragile a PRNU attribution is against this attack on their own pipelines. On a controlled multi-camera Monte-Carlo benchmark the attack reaches an arbitrary target PCE at a mean PSNR of 59.2 dB (visually lossless), yet the triangle test separates forgeries from innocent images with an area under the ROC curve of 0.999, detecting every forgery at a cohort-calibrated 5% false-positive operating point. We discuss why a fixed significance cut-off is not safe in casework, the limitations of synthetic validation, and the open problem of extending explainable detection to the modern, GAN-based generation of fingerprint-transfer attacks. The toolkit is released under the MIT license with an explicit dual-use statement.

papers.title: Exponential Double and Multiple Riordan Arrays as Fiber Products
papers.abstract: A double Riordan array has nonzero entries only in positions $(n,k)$ with $n+k$ even, and its even and odd parts are Riordan arrays with the same multiplier function. We develop this observation systematically, with the emphasis on exponential double and exponential multiple Riordan arrays. Using generalized Riordan arrays with respect to a sequence $(c_n)$, we show that the double Riordan group, the exponential double Riordan group, the multiple Riordan group, and the exponential multiple Riordan group are fiber products of (generalized) Riordan groups over the Lagrange group. For exponential double and exponential multiple Riordan arrays this yields product and inverse formulas without square or $\ell$th roots, valid over any field of characteristic zero; an abelian normal subgroup with quotient the Lagrange group and a corresponding splitting; subgroups isomorphic to the Riordan group; an iterated split-extension description of the multiple groups; and a characterization of elements of finite order, including the fact that over ${\mathbb R}$ every element of finite order is an involution. We show that the $\ell$th power of the production matrix is the direct sum of the production matrices of the compressions, give an explicit formula for it in terms of partial Bell polynomials, and characterize these arrays by a shared $A$-sequence. Finally, we reverse the construction. Two Riordan arrays with a common multiplier can always be interleaved into a unique double Riordan array, and into an ordinary Riordan array exactly when their first functions satisfy one more condition. Examples include Pascal-, Catalan-, Morgan--Voyce-, and ballot-type arrays.

papers.title: Multitime Equilibration and Multitime Mpemba Effects
papers.abstract: Equilibration of a quantum state leaves open whether its response to later interventions has also equilibrated. We establish multitime equilibration for a continuous process on a fixed observation window, retaining the autonomous system--environment dynamics and all internal time differences. A finite-time mean-square bound controls the full continuous-process norm through the effective energy dimension and energy-gap correlations. A factorial temporal-order bound lifts fixed-sector convergence to the full process, while a process-visible spectral measure distinguishes mean-square from pointwise equilibration. This framework defines multitime Mpemba effects by comparing preparations relative to one stationary process. In a semicircle-spectrum model, a preparation filter changes the decay exponent from $3/2$ to $5/2$ in every fixed sector and in the summed norm, despite a larger initial distance. A fixed unitary control and terminal measurement exhibit the same exponent improvement in their output probabilities. Noncommuting baths and a many-body spin environment separate this all-sector mechanism from selective finite-time acceleration.

papers.title: One-bubble stability, reduced coefficients, and threshold compactness for the Escobar functional
papers.abstract: Let $(M^n,g)$ be a smooth compact manifold with nonempty boundary and coercive conformal energy. For $n\ge5$, in a conformal representative with $H_g=0$, we prove quantitative stability near a concentrating boundary bubble whose center stays away from the umbilic locus. The norm of the constrained gradient controls the distance to the standard bubble family with sharp exponent $1/2$, and the distance to the Lyapunov--Schmidt corrected family linearly. In the same one-bubble neighborhood, at energies at least the sharp hemisphere value $S_\ast$, the distance to the standard family is also controlled linearly. These estimates follow from the exact reduced quadratic coefficient and the scale-derivative expansion of the reduced functional. The same scale equation shows that sequences of critical points at $S_\ast$ can concentrate only at umbilic points. For $n\ge3$, a profile decomposition without a sign assumption gives Palais--Smale compactness between $S_\ast$ and the first mixed level $(S_\ast^{n-1}+Y^{n-1})^{1/(n-1)}$, where $Y=C^*_{\text{Esc}}(M,g)$, and this endpoint is sharp. Between $S_\ast$ and the two-bubble level, we characterize noncompact levels by the lower critical values. For $n\ge7$, we obtain the fourth-order reduced expansion at umbilic centers. Under local total umbilicity, we evaluate the correction exactly, determine the conformal weight of the reduced coefficient, and obtain the optimal algebraic comparison with the squared ambient Weyl norm.

papers.title: When Does Cross-View Consistency Matter in Multi-View Appearance Augmentation? A Controlled Study for Visuomotor Policies
papers.abstract: Multi-view visual augmentation often seeks consistency across cameras, but it is unclear which forms of consistency matter for downstream control. We use simulation-state replay to manipulate cross-view coupling while preserving the per-camera perturbation distributions, physical trajectories, and action labels. Across seven LIBERO manipulation tasks, marginal-matched changes in global appearance, ghost injection, and target color have small average costs for a late-fusion Diffusion Policy: point estimates are near zero or negative, and the largest upper endpoint of the 90% posterior credible intervals is 2.55 percentage points. In contrast, geometrically anti-coupled observations reduce success by 3.30 percentage points relative to coupled observations (90% CrI [0.64, 6.28]), with displacement magnitude, direction marginals, and the number of affected views matched. Camera interventions reveal substantial dependence on wrist-view geometry, while feature analysis shows appearance sensitivity patterns associated with the factors randomized during training. ACT shows a higher target-color cost estimate than DP, with uncertainty that includes zero and sensitivity to task composition. Within the tested tasks and policy configurations, these findings motivate selective consistency constraints: appearance coupling can sometimes be relaxed, whereas task-relevant geometry and cross-view spatial correspondence warrant protection.

papers.title: Stage-wise Lineage-aware Dropout for Sparse-View 3D Gaussian Splatting
papers.abstract: Sparse-view 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) is prone to overfitting because only a limited number of images are available to constrain scene geometry. Dropout is one regularization strategy for alleviating this problem. We introduce the concept of a lineage family to describe a set of Gaussian primitives derived from the same founder through cloning or splitting operations. The founder Gaussians refer to all Gaussian primitives generated during initialization. Descendants within the same family often jointly contribute to the refinement of adjacent local regions. However, dropping individual Gaussians can be less effective due to the compensation effect from neighboring Gaussians for the dropped ones. To address this issue, we propose Stage-wise Lineage-aware Dropout(SLD), which applies lineage-family dropout during the structural regularization stage and switches to individual dropout during the later refinement stage. We further propose Lineage-Balanced Densification(LBD), which operates during densification by constructing an expanded candidate pool and reallocating the densification budget according to the mean gradient scores and existing descendant sizes of different families. Experiments on the LLFF, MipNeRF360, and Blender datasets show that the proposed framework achieves competitive performance in sparse-view reconstruction

papers.title: Superfluid: Local AI Server for Distributed LLM Inference
papers.abstract: Running large language models (LLMs) on local devices keeps data private, removes per-token cost, cuts network latency, and keeps working without a connection. Two shifts now strain how such models are served. On one device, several agents share a locally served model with an interactive user. Across devices, a developer or small team often owns several capable machines from different vendors, which sit idle most of the day because every local server serves one runtime on one machine. We present Superfluid, an open-source LLM server built for local inference at both scales. On one device, Superfluid drives llama.cpp, MLX, or BaseRT in isolated worker processes through one scheduler that moves interactive requests ahead of agent work, computes a prompt shared by many requests once, and writes every token to a durable log before it reaches the client. Across devices, one Superfluid server turns a fleet of machines into a single API endpoint. Machines with different hardware serve copies of the same model, receive work according to their measured speed, and can join or fail under load without losing a request. For Qwen3.8-27B on an Apple M5 Pro, a chat sent while eight agents are working receives its first token in 1.5 s, against 291-612 s on llama-server, Ollama, and mlx_lm.server. On six machines from three chip vendors serving 64 simulated users for one hour, Superfluid answers all 5,041 requests while machines join one at a time and one is killed and rejoins; throughput grows from 112 to 534 tok/s and the median first-token time falls from 99 to 12 s. On twelve Mac Studio M3 Ultras it sustains 10,656 tok/s across 38,563 requests from 384 agents without a failure. Superfluid is available under the Apache-2.0 licence at https://github.com/basecompute/superfluid.

papers.title: See Every Block Once: Variance-Reduced Post-Training for Masked Diffusion Language Models
papers.abstract: Policy gradient methods are widely used to align large language model outputs with human preferences, but the log-likelihoods they require cannot be directly computed in Masked Diffusion Language Models (MDLMs). MDLM post-training therefore relies on a surrogate objective based on the Evidence Lower Bound (ELBO), and recent work estimates a blockwise variant of this objective via Monte Carlo methods to support blockwise generation. However, existing estimation schemes randomly sample the block index, so they may evaluate the same block more than once and leave some blocks unevaluated. This introduces variance arising from block selection into the estimates. In this work, we propose a full-block estimator that evaluates every block exactly once and averages the results. We theoretically show that the proposed estimator remains unbiased while eliminating the between-group variance arising from block selection, thereby achieving lower variance than the baseline for the same sample size. In experiments on five benchmarks spanning mathematics, planning, and coding, our method achieves the highest accuracy on four benchmarks and outperforms the random block sampling baseline by an average of 12.79 points.

papers.title: VACO: Vertex-Aligned Decoding for Dense Hand Contact Estimation from a Single Image
papers.abstract: Dense hand contact estimation from a single RGB image is a foundational primitive for dexterous manipulation and 3D interaction analysis. Direct predictors typically decode the entire per-vertex contact map from one shared query, leaving individual vertices ungrounded in the image and smearing contact across adjacent, non-touching surfaces. We present VACO, a vertex-aligned decoder in which each MANO vertex samples local image features at its projected location. A hand-reconstruction backbone, jointly trained for reconstruction and contact, predicts these locations at inference without an auxiliary reconstructor. Training uses noise-perturbed ground-truth projections and end-to-end feature adaptation to improve robustness and contact-sensitive features. A single VACO checkpoint sets a new state of the art on five benchmarks spanning hand-object, hand-human, hand-scene, and bimanual interactions. It improves F1 by +20.7 pp over the strongest prior direct predictor on Hi4D and generalizes to the held-out HOT3D and HOCap, with gains of +5.5 and +2.7 pp. The resulting contact predictions also improve downstream HOI reconstruction.

papers.title: Compiling Matrix Formulas to Quantum Block Encodings
papers.abstract: Realizing the promise of quantum applications such as chemistry or fluid dynamics requires building quantum circuits that efficiently encode and manipulate exponentially large matrices. This process forces researchers to grapple with the reality that a matrix expressible as one equation on paper can map to thousands of bit-level quantum logic gates, historically written by hand. Even worse, it often ends with a discovery that the needed resources grow so quickly with matrix size that the quantum algorithm loses its asymptotic speedup. In this work, we present MARBLE, a language that automatically synthesizes an efficient circuit from the publication-style formula for the entries of a matrix. MARBLE algebraically rewrites programs into symbolic combinations of simpler matrices that have known circuit realizations. It analyzes costs of possible representations, notably the subnormalization term that dominates time complexity. It then emits an OpenQASM circuit and certifies whether its cost is poly-logarithmic in problem size, as required by quantum algorithms. When evaluated on quantum applications ranging from fluid dynamics to physical Hamiltonians, MARBLE matches or surpasses 37 of 39 published baselines. On the low end, it automatically matches many theoretically optimal circuits, and on the high end, it improves on a published construction in fluid dynamics by 10,487x in subnormalization. MARBLE produces exponentially smaller circuits than the leading tool FABLE, and it successfully compiles matrices whose dimensions exceed 2^100 within five seconds on a laptop.

papers.title: Graph Neural Network Prediction of Frequency Nadir and RoCoF Under Topology Variations
papers.abstract: Accurate prediction of frequency dynamics under varying network topologies is essential for rapid frequency security assessment, whereas repeated electromagnetic transient (EMT) simulations are computationally intensive. This paper develops a topology-aware graph neural network with a radial basis function Kolmogorov-Arnold network (RBF-KAN) regression head, termed RK-GNN, to predict frequency nadir and maximum absolute rate of change of frequency (RoCoF). Scenarios combine load scaling, regional load redistribution, and generator redispatch with intact, N-1, and N-2 transmission topologies. After checks for network connectivity, generator reference limits, and numerical consistency, the retained scenarios are simulated in PSCAD to construct the reference dataset. The RK-GNN is evaluated against a conventional deep neural network (DNN) and a baseline GNN. On the IEEE 39-bus system, the RK-GNN reduces the mean absolute errors (MAEs) of nadir and RoCoF by 48% and 59% relative to the DNN and by 42% and 61% relative to the baseline GNN. Incorporating the bridge indicator and disturbance hop distance yields further MAE reductions of 27% and 54%. These results show that the proposed topology-aware architecture provides accurate prediction of both frequency metrics under varying topologies and substantially reduces the need for repeated EMT simulations.

papers.title: Efficient Genotype Classification from 3D MRI in ADPKD via Density-Aware Point Sampling and E(3)-invariance
papers.abstract: Early detection of genetic kidney diseases, especially autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD), is crucial because certain genotypes such as truncating PKD1 mutations cause rapid kidney growth and early progression to end-stage kidney disease. MRI-based genotype inference is a potential low-cost complement to genetic testing. However, although many deep learning methods have been developed for classifying various MR images, applying them to ADPKD remains challenging: (1) abdominal MR images are generally too large to be handled by deep learning models designed for smaller images like brain MRI, and (2) the amount of labeled data for ADPKD genetic mutations is insufficient to train deep learning models. In order to address these challenges, we propose E3PN, an efficient 3D MRI-based ADPKD genotype classification network that relies on point sampling and E(3)-invariance. We utilize a point representation of 3D MRI, which consumes less GPU memory than a voxel representation. For further memory efficiency, 3D points are sampled from a mixture distribution over the two kidneys in each image. Since E(3)-invariance has been shown to improve data efficiency, we also incorporate it into our model through coordinate canonicalization. On our ADPKD dataset, E3PN trains 163 times faster and uses 103x less GPU memory than a 3D ResNet, while also improving F1 from 0.165 to 0.226 over both baselines. These results establish a first benchmark for five-way ADPKD genotype classification from 3D MRI and show that point sampling and coordinate canonicalization yield two-orders-of-magnitude efficiency gains with a modest but consistent improvement in F1.

papers.title: Convergence analysis of physics-informed neural networks for subdiffusion
papers.abstract: Physics-informed neural networks have emerged as mesh-free solvers for partial differential equations, yet their rigorous convergence theory for time-fractional problems remains limited. We present a convergence analysis of PINNs for linear subdiffusion equations and for the associated backward problem of recovering the initial data from terminal observations. To address the nonlocality and weakly singular kernels of fractional derivatives, we introduce a discretization-based PINN framework built on some popular time-stepping schemes satisfying discrete maximal regularity, including backward Euler, BDF2, L1, and fractional CN schemes. This approach avoids the exact evaluation of fractional derivatives at training points while preserving the stability structure needed for convergence analysis. For the forward problem, we prove that, under the natural fractional maximal-regularity condition $u\in W^{α,p}(0,T;L^2(Ω))\cap L^p(0,T;H^2(Ω)\cap H_0^1(Ω))$, the piecewise linear temporal reconstructions of PINN-loss minimizers converge to the exact solution. This result avoids the higher-order regularity assumptions on the exact solution that are often imposed in existing PINN convergence analyses. We also verify the required discrete maximal regularity and consistency properties for the aforementioned popular time discretizations. We then extend the analysis to the backward subdiffusion problem and establish convergence of the regularized recovery of the initial data from terminal observations, despite its ill-posedness. Numerical experiments for both forward and backward problems support the theoretical results, demonstrate the necessity of regularization, and show that $L^2$-type losses alone are generally insufficient.
